## Setup — environment variables
Set these in n8n (self-hosted: Settings > Environment Variables, or your .env):

- `SUPABASE_URL`
- `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`  (service role, NOT the anon key — this workflow writes to protected tables)
- `DEZGO_API_KEY`

Also run the `decrement_credit` SQL function from the schema before using this workflow.

## Requires the 'jimp' npm package
Self-hosted n8n: set `NODE_FUNCTION_ALLOW_EXTERNAL=jimp` and run `npm install jimp` inside the n8n container, then restart.

The Code node supports **both Jimp v0 and v1** — v1 renamed `getBufferAsync`, `MIME_JPEG`, `AUTO` and the positional `resize()`, so writing to v0's API alone will throw on a modern install.

## Failure path
Every step that can realistically throw — image download, Dezgo, colour correction, storage upload — routes its error output here, so the render row is set to `failed` instead of being left on `processing`.

The app polls that row. Without this, any error left the user watching a spinner forever.

## What the app sends here
`{ render_id, user_id, photo_url, color_hex, color_name, colors[], surface, prompt, brand_logo_url, brand_contact }`

Correction call:
`{ render_id, user_id, correction_prompt, surface, brand_logo_url, brand_contact }`

`surface` is the "Paint the" text. `colors[]` holds up to three picks; `color_hex` is the single colour the LAB correction pass locks to.
